To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the CUVAF in keratoconus is significantly lower compared with control subjects.
the conjunctival autofluorescence in keratoconus patients is lower than in healthy individuals and that the aCXL does not change the CUVAF in keratoconous patients.
The eyes undergoing accelerated cross linking procedure showed no difference of CUVAF but the keratoconic individuals should be under strict follow up to reveal UV related eye diseases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the CUVAF as a marker of the cornea and conjunctiva UV irradiation.
the possibility of CUVAF as a measure of UV exposure and the possibility of its application in keratoconus diagnostics.
the possibility of CUVAF to be used in the follow up of keratoconic and other patients undergoing aCXL procedure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CUVAF is a useful tool for the assessment of keratoconic cornea.
CUVAF is a reliable marker to monitor the UV exposure in keratoconus patients.
the CUVAF is a reliable and useful method to assess the UV damage of the conjunctiva.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CUVAF is a good marker of the keratoconic eye and it can be useful in monitoring the keratoconus progression. It
the conjunctival autofluorescence can be used to measure the UV exposure in keratoconus patients.
aCXL procedure has no influence on the CUVAF.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CUVAF can be used to measure UV exposure in keratoconus and other ocular surface diseases.
aCXL does not cause significant changes in the CUVAF of the conjunctiva.
the conjunctiva is a good target to assess UV related ocular damage in keratoconus patients.
